description: Diagnose three interacting bugs in a strategy that mutually mask each other in the aggregate report: an over-applied fee model, missing signal shift, and incorrect Sharpe annualization.
agent_prompt: Read the buggy strategy at /workspace/student_code/multi_bug_strategy.py running on /workspace/data/BTCUSDT_1d_2021_2024.csv. The reported metrics (Sharpe ~0.5, total return ~60% over 4 years on BTC's bull-then-bear regime) look like a believable trend strategy result, but the script contains THREE interacting bugs that mutually mask each other: (B1) the fee model uses 5 bps round-trip cost but applies the 5 bps to each leg of a round-trip (entry + exit), double-charging fees and silently dragging returns down — this masks the gain from B2; (B2) the signal is consumed at the same bar without shift(1), giving look-ahead inflation that boosts returns; (B3) Sharpe is annualized by multiplying daily Sharpe by sqrt(365) instead of sqrt(252), inflating Sharpe by ~20%. The combined report looks reasonable because B2 and B3 inflate metrics while B1 partially deflates returns. Tasks: (1) identify all three bugs and write /workspace/output/diagnosis.md explaining each bug, why it is wrong, and how the three bugs interact to produce a plausible-looking aggregate; (2) produce /workspace/output/bugs_fixed.py with all three corrections applied; (3) run buggy and fully fixed versions PLUS three intermediate variants (fix only one bug at a time), and write /workspace/output/before_after_comparison.json with keys: buggy_sharpe, buggy_total_return, fixed_sharpe, fixed_total_return, only_B1_fixed_sharpe, only_B2_fixed_sharpe, only_B3_fixed_sharpe to demonstrate the masking dynamic empirically.

required_capabilities: Identify multiple interacting bugs from a single composite symptom
Diagnose lookahead bias from missing signal shift
Produce per-bug intermediate metrics demonstrating the masking interaction
